metaDescription: Estimate blood alcohol concentration and the time until it reaches zero from drinks, body weight, sex and hours since the first drink, using the Widmark...
intro: Estimate blood alcohol from your drinks, weight and time.
why:
List your drinks as count, millilitres and percent alcohol, then enter your weight, sex and the hours since your first drink. The page uses the Widmark formula, BAC = A / (r x W) - beta x t, with alcohol at 0.789 g per ml, r of 0.68 for men and 0.55 for women, and an elimination rate you can change (default 0.015 g/dL per hour).

It is a rough guide only. Food, medication, drinking pace and body differences move the real figure a lot. It assumes all the alcohol is absorbed at once, so it overstates the peak for slow drinking. It is not a test of whether you can drive. Do not drive after drinking.
howTo: Type one drink per line, for example 2 x 330 5.
Choose sex and enter weight and hours.
Adjust the elimination rate if you wish.
Read the estimate and the time to zero.

faq.q: Can I use this to decide if I can drive?
faq.a: No. Never use it for that. The estimate can be wrong in both directions, and legal limits differ by country.

faq.q: Why do women get a lower r?
faq.a: Widmark factors reflect average body water share, which differs between men and women on average. Individuals vary a lot.
